आदिक: Ādika m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 7, 2.
आपूरण: Āpūraṇa m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 10, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 13. 6.
आप्त: Āpta m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 12, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
आमाहठ: Āmāhaṭha m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, one of those offered in the सर्पसत्र; description: ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 15, 1, 13.
आयु: Āyu m.: King of the frogs (मण्डूक-राज). His daughter Suśobhanā 3. 190. 37; he requested king Parikṣit of the Ikṣvāku family not to kill innocent frogs 3. 190 33; gave his daughter in marriage to Parikṣit, but also cursed her for having cheated before many kings 3. 190. 39-40.
आरुणि: Āruṇi1 m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, one of those offered in the सर्पसत्र; description: ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 17, 1, 13.
Āruṇi2 m.: A mythical bird. Son of Vinatā (वैनतेय) 1. 59. 39; present among those who greeted the birth of Arjuna 1. 114. 62.
आर्यक: Āryaka m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 11, 1. A. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7. B. Also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū. C. His grand-son Sumukha 5. 101. 19, 23; Nārada requested Āryaka to accept Mātali's dau-ghter Guṇakeśī for his grand-son Sumukha 5. 102. 6-11; Āryaka distressed because his son Cikura was eaten by Vainateya (Garuda), and similar fate awaited Sumukha 5. 102. 14-16; his purpose achieved, he was happy to return home when Indra granted long life to Sumukha 5. 102. 27, 29.
आग्नि: Āgni-(astra) nt.: Name of a missile 5. 140. 6. [See Āgneyāstra1].
आग्नेयास्त्र: Āgneyāstra1 nt.: Name of a missile; referred to as Āgni-astra in उभे चैवाग्नि-मारुते 5. 140. 6. A. Origin and succession: Arjuna told Gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa that Bṛhaspati gave it first to Bharadvāja, Bharadvāja to sage Agniveśya, Agniveśya to Droṇa, and Droṇa to Arjuna 1. 158. 26-27; 1. 121. 6-7; but Arjuna told Uttara that he obtained Āgneyāstra from god Agni 4. 56. 14; when Gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa expressed his desire to learn the अस्त्र, Arjuna taught it to him in exchange of the Gandharva horses (गन्धर्-वजाः … हयाः 1. 158. 51) 1. 158. 54-55; Arjuna taught it to the Gandharva with due rites (यथाविधि) 1. 174. 3; when Arjuna requested Indra for heavenly weapons, Indra assured him that he would give him all the heavenly missiles, आग्नेय and the rest (आग्नेयानि च सर्वाणि) after Arjuna had satisfied god Mahādeva 1. 225. 12, 10; among the epic heroes, besides Droṇa and Arjuna, its use was known also to Kṛṣṇa (6. 116. 38; also see Āgneyāstra2), Bhīṣma, Karṇa and Aśvatthāman (7. 166. 2) [See the section C below]. B. Description: divine (दिव्य) 6. 116. 38; 7. 73. 46; very dreadful (महा-घोर) 7. 73. 46; very frightful (सुदारुण) 4. 59. 21; irresistible even by the gods (देवैर् अपि सुदुर्धर्षम्) 7. 172. 14. C. Its use in war and its effects: 1. In the epic war: (i) when used by Karṇa against Arjuna, it gave to Karṇa's bow a fiery look and it released fiery arrows; Arjuna apparently combated it with the same kind of अस्त्र (अस्त्रं अस्त्रेण संवार्य) 7. 31. 51-52; (ii) used by Droṇa against Yuyudhāna (Sātyaki); this was combated by Sātyaki with Vāruṇāstra 7. 73. 46; (iii) Bhāradvāja (Droṇa) used Āgneya and other heavenly missiles against Yudhiṣṭhira which were ren-dered ineffective by Yudhiṣṭhira 7. 132. 29-30; (iv) Aśvatthāman used it against Arjuna; when released, it produced a shower of arrows (शरवर्षम् अजायत 7. 172. 16; शरवृष्टयः 7. 172. 22); cold winds blew, sun lost its lustre, clouds rained blood, all beings became restless; the arrows were fiery and produced good deal of heat; they burnt down enemies, elephants, horses and chariots; the god Fire burnt the army like the Saṃvartaka fire at the end of the aeon 7. 172. 16-27; the whole army, including Arjuna, could not be seen due to the darkness; the like of the अस्त्र released by Aśvatthāman was never seen before by Saṃjaya and his colleagues 7. 172. 30-31; Arjuna combated it with Brāhma Astra 7. 172. 14, 32; it was meant to be used by Arjuna in the war 5. 140. 6 (here referred to as Āgni instead of Āgneya). 2. Outside the epic war: (i) Arjuna used it against Gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa; when released, it burnt down the excellent chariot of Aṅgāra-parṇa, and he fell down, head downwards, as he swooned due to the lustre of the missile 1. 158. 28, 29, 37; (ii) used by Droṇa (besides using other divine missiles) against Arjuna at the time of the cattle-raid; Arjuna combated it with his Āgneyāstra 4. 53. 48; (iii) on the same occasion used by Bhīṣma and Arjuna against each other to combat each other's missiles 4. 59. 21; (iv) in his fight with Citrasena and the Gandharvas Arjuna killed thousands of Gandharvas with Āgneyāstra 3. 234. 7; when released once again, the Gandharvas, afflicted by heat, were dejected 3. 234. 17; (v) at the time of displaying his skill in the use of missiles, Arjuna produced fire by releasing Āgneyāstra 1. 125. 19; (vi) employed by Bhīṣma against Rāma (Jāmadagnya); it was rendered in-effective by the counter-use of Vāruṇāstra 5. 181. 12. D. Mode of use: The normal arrows were supposed to be infused by this अस्त्र (अस्त्रे ते वारुणाग्नेये ताभ्यां बाणसमाहिते 7. 73. 48) by reciting मन्त्रस् over it (अनुमन्त्र्य 5. 181. 12, अभिमन्त्र्य 7. 172. 15); Aśvatthāman also sipped water (वार्य् उपस्पृश्य 7. 172. 14) before reciting मन्त्रस्। E. Status: Inferior to Śivā's Pāśupatāstra 13. 14. 127.

Āgneyāstra2 nt.: Name of a missile identified with Kṛṣṇa's Sudarśana cakra. Received by Kṛṣṇa from God Fire बेफ़ोरे the burning of the Khāṇḍava forest 1. 216. 21; however, it is said that Kṛṣṇa got it from God Fire अफ़्तेर् satisfying him 7. 10. 21; released by Kṛṣṇa against Śālva 3. 23. 28. [See Sudarśana].
आङ्गिरस: Āṅgirasa nt.: Name of a bow used by Droṇa. Described as heavenly (दिव्य), Droṇa used it to fight a duel with Dhṛṣṭadyumna; Droṇa shot arrows with it which looked like ब्रह्मदण्ड 7. 164. 122.

Āṅgirasa m.: Name of the planet Jupiter. Arjuna and Aśvatthāman, who had the lustre of Śukra and Āṅgirasa, fought with each other as the two planets would do in heaven for a नक्षत्र (ततः सम-भवद् युद्धम् शुक्राङ्गिरसवर्चसोः । नक्षत्रम् अभितो व्योम्नि शुक्राङ्गिरसयोर् इव ॥ ) 8. 12. 48 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 8. 17. 1: नक्षत्रम् अभितः नक्षत्रम् लक्षीकृत्य).
आजगव: Ājagava1 nt.: Name of the bow of king Māndhātṛ. He received it miraculously soon after his birth (from Indra ? 3. 126. 27, 29, 32) 3. 126. 31. [See Ājagava2].
Ājagava2 adj.: The Gāṇḍīva bow of Arjuna so described 7. 120. 86, (85). [lit. ‘one which was covered with the skin of a goat and a cow ?’].
आथर्वण: Ātharvaṇa nt.: Name (?) of a missile. Karṇa had received it from Rāma (Jāma-dagnya); described as ‘of great prowess’ (महामहिमन्) and ‘killer of enemies’ (अरिविनाशन); by using it Karṇa blew away the burning missile of Arjuna 8. 66. 3.

Ātharvaṇa1 adj.: related to Atharvan, i. e. the Atharvaveda. When all the sages took the oath to prove that they had not stolen Agastya's lotus stalks, Śakra, when his turn came, uttered a benediction (instead of a curse) and said, among other things, “Let him who has stolen your stalks be like a Brāh-maṇa (विप्र) who takes bath after com-pleting the study of the Ātharvaṇa Veda” (आथर्वणं वेदम् अधीत्य विप्रः स्नायेत यः पुष्करम् आददाति) 13. 96. 44.

Ātharvaṇa2 adj.: A मन्त्र related to the Atharvaveda. These मन्त्रस् were used to cure the poison of a scorpion, or various other kinds of poisons (मद्रके संगतं नास्ति हतं वृश्चिकतो भवेत् । आथर्वणेन मन्त्रेण सर्वा शान्तिः कृता भवेत् ॥ इति वृश्चिकद-ष्टस्य नानाविषहतस्य च । कुर्वन्ति भेषजं प्राज्ञाः सत्यं तच् चापि दृश्यते ॥ ) 8. 27. 83, 84.
Ātharvaṇa3 adj.: A remedy prescribed in the Atharvaveda. प्रज्ञाशरेणाभिहतस्य जन्तोः … नाथ्-अर्वणा नाप्य् अगदाः सुसिद्धाः 5. 37. 54 [Nī., however, आथर्वणा वेदमन्त्राः on Bom. Ed. 5. 37. 58].
आदित्यास्त्र: Ādityāstra nt.: Name of a missile. Used by Arjuna to dry up the floods of waters created by Śakuni with his माया 7. 29. 25.
आप्लुत: Āpluta nt.: One of the twenty-one movements (मार्ग) used while fighting with a sword. Dhṛṣṭadyumna adopted it in turn while attacking Droṇa 7. 164. 147-148.
आविद्ध: Āviddha nt.: One of the twenty-one movements (मार्ग) used while fighting with a sword. Dhṛṣṭadyumna adopted it in turn while attacking Droṇa 7. 164. 147-148.
आसुर: Āsura1 adj.: A kind of व्यूह (arrange-ment of the army) known to the Asuras. Bhīṣma knew different kinds of व्यूहस्, one of them being आसुर 6. 19. 2; he arranged his army every day a different way, one of the ways being आसुर 6. 20. 18; 6. 104. 16; Dhṛṣṭadyumna also knew how to arrange the army the आसुर way and in other ways 5. 56. 11.
Āsura2 adj.: A kind of missile known to the Asuras. Ghaṭotkaca knew different kinds of mis-siles some of them being the ones used by the Asuras 7. 148. 36 (also cf. 7. 148. 41).
आस्यमोदक: Āsyamodaka nt.: Name of a missile (अस्त्र). One of the eight अस्त्रस् of Arjuna recounted by Rāma (Jāmadagnya) to Dur-yodhana; when struck by any one of these, the victim died, or became insane, or lost consciousness, or he slept, or jumped up, or vomited, or passed urine, or he wept or laughed incessantly; (perhaps Āsyamodaka produced only the last effect of making the adversary weep or laugh incessantly ?) 5. 94. 38-40.
आगस्त्य: Āgastya nt.: Name of an आख्यान। Listed among the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan; the आख्यान narrates incidents in Agastya's life which include devouring of the demon Vātāpi and the sage's approaching his wife Lopāmudrā for a child 1. 2. 114; 3. 108. 19; related to the incidents narrated in the Adhyāyas 3. 94-103.

Āgastya m. (pl.): Name of a family of ऋषिस्। Described as illustrious (महाभाग) 3. 27. 8; Baka Dālbhya showed to Yudhi-ṣṭhira that in the Dvaitavana many Brā-hmaṇas, among whom he named Āgastyas, had associated themselves with him and, protected by him, were practising धर्म (पश्य द्वैतवने पार्थ … चरन्ति धर्-मं पुण्ये ऽस्मिंस् त्वया गुप्ता धृत-व्रताः । … आगस्त्याश् च महाभागाः) 3. 27. 6-8; (for other details about the sages, Brāhmaṇas gathered in the Dvaitavana, see Ātreya (2) below).
आजगर: Ājagara nt.: Name of the 36th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 44, 33, 70. Related to Adhyāyas 3. 173-178.
आदिपर्वन्: Ādiparvan nt.: Name of the first पर्वन् of the Bhārata in a total of eighteen major पर्वन्स् 1. 2. 95, 71. Its contents are summarized in 1. 2. 71-95; (1. 1. 67-83; 1. 55. 6-37); accord-ing to the Parvasaṃgrahaparvan it has 218 अध्यायस् and 7984 श्लोकस् as counted by the great sage Vyāsa (संख्याते परमर्-षिणा … व्यासेन) 1. 2. 95-96.
आदिवंशावतारण: Ādivaṃśāvatāraṇa nt.: Name of the 6th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 34, 33, 70. It narrates the origins of various Vipras, as also of the sage Dvaipāyana (Vyāsa), the partial descent of the gods, and the origins of the Daityas, Dānavas, and of mighty Yakṣas, also of Nāgas, serpents, Gandharvas, and birds, and of various other beings 1. 2. 75-77; it comprises Adhyāyas 1. 54-61.
आनुशासनिक: Ānuśāsanika nt.: Name of the 89th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 65, 33, 70. This is the 13th पर्वन् in the list of the 18 parvans of the Bhārata [See Anuśāsana]
आपद्धर्म: Āpaddharma m.: Name of the 87th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 64, 33, 70. It forms a sub-पर्वन् of the 12th Śāntiparvan and comprises Adhyāyas 12. 129-167; it lays down the emergency duties which point to particular time as the cause for their prescription; knowing these a man becomes perfectly omniscient (आपद्-धर्माश् च तत्रैव कालहेतुप्रदर्शकाः । यान् बुद्ध्वा पुरुषः सम्यक् सर्वज्ञत्वम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥ ) 1. 2. 198 [Nī., however, says कालो दुर्भिक्षादिर् हेतुर् वैररोगादिश् च तत्प्रदर्शिनः देशकालाद्यपेक्षया वर्-तितव्यम् इत्य् अर्थः Bom. Ed. 1. 2. 327].
आभिषेचनिक: Ābhiṣecanika nt.: Name of the 83rd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 62, 33, 70. It deals with the consecration of Dhar-marāja (Yudhiṣṭhira) 1. 2. 62 (cf. Śānti-parvan Adhyāya 40).
आयुर्वेद: Āyurveda m.: Name of the science of medicine. Even the physicians studying the Āyur-veda themselves or their families are afflicted by diseases and although they take various decoctions (कषायस्) and clarified butter (सर्पींषि) for cure, they cannot avoid death 12. 28. 44-45;—Kṛṣṇa tells Arjuna that his many names have been recounted by great sages in the Sāṃkhya, the Yogaśāstra and the Āyurveda 12. 328. 9; those versed in the Āyurveda give the name Tridhātu to Kṛṣṇa, since the body has three constituents [bile (पित्त), phlegm (श्लेष्मन्) and wind (वायु)] and is sustained by them and when they are wasted away the body is emaciated 12. 330. 21-22 [Nī. explains Tridhātu as त्रयो धातव उपाधिभुताः सन्त्य् अस्य स त्रिधातुः on Bom. Ed. 12. 342. 87].
आरणेय: Āraṇeya nt.: Name of the 44th पर्-वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 48, 33, 70. In the brief enumeration of the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan it is called an उपाख्यान where god Dharma instructed his son (Yudhiṣṭhira), and then the Pāṇḍavas having received the boon (from him) went towards the west 1. 2. 127; related to the अध्यायस् 3. 295-299.
आरण्यक: Āraṇyaka1 nt.: Name of the 29th पर्-वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa 1. 2. 42, 33, 70. Referred to as ‘where the citizens follow-ed Yudhiṣṭhira (when he started to go to the forest)’ while narrating the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 105; it comprises अध्यायस् 3. 1-11.

Āraṇyaka2 nt.: Name of the third पर्वन् among the eighteen major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata 1. 2. 105, 128. Described as large (महत्) 1. 2. 105; according to the Parvasaṃgrahaparvan it contains 269 अध्यायस् and 11664 श्लोकस् as counted by the great sage (Vyāsa) (सं-ख्याते परमर्षिणा) 1. 2. 128-129; its contents are summarized in 1. 2. 105-127; Arjuna, when he vowed to kill Jayadratha and then received the Pāśupata astra from Śiva, remembered the boon he had received from him and the sight he had obtained in the Āraṇyaka (i. e. in the Āraṇyakaparvan or during the stay in the forest ?) (ततः प्रीतं भवं ज्ञात्वा स्मृतिमान् अर्जुनस् तदा । वरम् आरण्यके दत्तं दर्शनं शङ्करस्य च) 7. 57. 78.
आर्तिमत्: Ārtimant m.: Name of a मन्त्र (?), of a sage (?). One who remembers the Ārtimant मन्त्र along with the Asita and the Sunī-tha has no fear from serpents either by day or at night 1. 53. 23 (असितम् चार्तिमन्-तं च सुनीथं चापि यः स्मरेत् । दिवा वा यदि वा रात्रौ नास्य सर्पभयं भवेत् (cf. Nī. Bom Ed. 1. 58. 23: प्रसङ्गात् सर्पभयनिवर्तका मन्त्रान् पठति । असितम् इत्यादीन्). [See Asita and Sunītha]
आर्तिमन्त्: Ārtimant m.: Name of a मन्त्र (?), of a sage (?). One who remembers the Ārtimant मन्त्र along with the Asita and the Sunī-tha has no fear from serpents either by day or at night 1. 53. 23 (असितम् चार्तिमन्-तं च सुनीथं चापि यः स्मरेत् । दिवा वा यदि वा रात्रौ नास्य सर्पभयं भवेत् (cf. Nī. Bom Ed. 1. 58. 23: प्रसङ्गात् सर्पभयनिवर्तका मन्त्रान् पठति । असितम् इत्यादीन्). [See Asita and Sunītha]
आश्रमवास: Āśramavāsa1 m.: Name of the 93rd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 67 (पर्व चाश्रमवासाख्यम्), 33, 70. It comprises अध्यायस् 15. 1-35.

Āśramavāsa2 m. (= Āśramavāsika nt. so called in the colophons to the अध्यायस् 15, 30, 32, 35, 36, 37, 40, 43, 44, 46): Name of the 15th पर्वन् among the 18 major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata (तत आश्र-मवासाख्यं पर्व पञ्चदशं स्मृतम्) 1. 2. 212, 218. According to the Parvasaṃgrahaparvan it has 42 chapters (अध्यायस्) and 1506 stanzas (श्लोकस्) as counted by (Vyāsa) who sees the truth (संख्यातास् तत्त्वदर्शिना) 1. 2. 218-219; in this पर्वन् Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with Gāndhārī and Vidura, left the capital and went to the hermitage; they were followed by Pṛthā (Kuntī); in this hermitage the king saw, by the favour of the sage Kṛṣṇa (Vyāsa), his sons, grand-sons, and other kings and heroes, who were killed in battle, come back again; that was a wonder unsurpassed (आश्चर्यम् अनुत्तमम् 1. 2. 215); seeing it Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī abandoned grief and obtained high perfection (सिद्धिं परमिकां गतः 1. 2. 215); in this पर्वन्, we hear of Vidura and Saṃjaya going to the next world; in this पर्वन्, Yudhiṣṭhira met Nārada and heard from him the great killing of the Vṛṣṇis (the Yādavas) 1. 2. 212-217.
आश्वमेधिक: Āśvamedhika nt.: Name of the 14th पर्वन् in the list of the 18 major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata (1. 2. 210) [See Aśva-medhika]
आस्तीक: Āstīka nt.: Name of the 5th पर्वन् (also referred to as आख्यान, कथा and पुराण इतिहास) in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parva-saṃgraha 1. 2. 34, 33, 70. Described as great (महद् आख्यानम् आस्तीकम्) 1. 13. 4, and attractive (कथाम् एताम् मनोरमाम् । आस्तीकस्य) 1. 13. 5; it comprises Adhyāyas 1. 13-53; in this sub-पर्वन् we are told about the birth of the snakes and of Garuḍa, the churning of the milky ocean, the origin of Uccaiśravas; it provides the setting for the narration of the story of the Bhāratas to Janamejaya, son of Parikṣit, who was offering the snake-sacrifice 1. 2. 73-74; according to some the Bhārata begins with the Āstīka (parvan) (मन्वादि भारतं केचिद् आस्तीकादि तथापरे) 1. 1. 50; Ruru wanted to know the life story of Āstīka (आस्तीक-चरित), and the narrative (आख्यान) was told to him by his father Pramati 1. 12. 3, 5; the elders called it an ancient इतिहास which was narrated by Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana (Vyāsa) to the sages in the Naimiṣa forest (इतिहासम् इमं वृद्धाः पुराणं परि-चक्षते) 1. 13. 6; narrated by Sūta Loma-harṣaṇa, pupil of Vyāsa, to the Brāhmaṇas at their request; his son Sūta Ugraśravas heard it from Lomaharṣaṇa and he, in turn, narrated it to Śaunaka 1. 13. 7-8, 45; Śaunaka again requested Sūta Ugraśravas to tell the story (कथा) of Āstīka in detail (सौते कथय ताम् एताम् विस्तरेण कथां पुनः । आस्तीकस्य कवेः साधोः शुश्रूषा परमा हि नः ॥ ) 1. 14. 1; the narrative of Āstīka confers long life (आयुष्-यम् इदम् आख्यानम् आस्तीकम्) 1. 14. 4; the आख्यान of Āstīka, his life-story (चरित), is exceedingly pious (धर्मिष्ठ), increases merit (of the listener) (पुण्यवर्धन), and is illustrious (श्रीमत्); one who recites it or listens to it from the very beginning shall have no danger from the snakes 1. 53. 25-26.
आग्नेय: Āgneya nt.: Name of the constellation Kṛttikā. One should not perform any rite for gods or पितृस् under the Āgneya constellation (दैवं पित्र्यम् अथापि च । न … कार्यं तथाग्नेये च भारत) 13. 107. 119. [See Kṛttikā]
आर्द्रा: Ārdrā f.: Name of a constellation. Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that if one gave as a gift, after fasting, कृसर mixed with sesamum oil, under the constella-tion Ārdrā one could get over difficulties and cross mountains having edges as sharp as a razor (आर्द्रायां कृसरं दत्त्वा तैलमि-श्रम् उपोषितः । नरस् तरति दुर्गाणि क्षुर-धारांश् च पर्वतान्) 13. 63. 8; Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that by offering a श्राद्ध (which is काम्य) under Ārdrā one could perform terrible deeds (क्रूरकर्मा … मानवो भवेत्) 13. 89. 3.
आश्लेषा: Āśleṣā f.: Name of a constellation. Nārada informed Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that one who gave as a gift under the con-stellation Āśleṣā silver (रूप्य) or a bull he became free from all dangers and overpowered his enemies 13. 63. 11; Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that by offering a श्राद्ध (which is काम्य) under the constellation Āśleṣā one got heroic sons 13. 89. 5.
आश्वयुज्: Āśvayuj m.: Name of the month (Āśvina). Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that if one, remaining pure and composed (शुचिर् आत्म-वान्), gave घृत to Vipras in the month of Āśvayuj the pleased Aśvinau gave him a handsome form (तस्मै प्रयच्छतो रूपम् प्रीतौ देवाव् इहाश्विनौ) 13. 64. 10; the sage Aṅgiras told Bhīṣma (13. 109. 9-10) that if one passed the month of Āśvayuj eating once a day he would have a large progeny, many vehicles, and many sons (तथैवाश्वयुजं मासम् एकभक्तेन यः क्षपेत् । प्रजावान् वाहनाढ्यश् च बहु-पुत्रश् च जायते) 13. 109. 28.
आषाढ: Āṣāḍha m.: Name of a month. Aṅgiras had told Bhīṣma (13. 109. 9-10) that if one diligently (अतन्द्रितः) took only one meal a day in the month of Āṣāḍha he had ample field produce, wealth and many sons (बहुधान्यो बहुधनो बहुपुत्रश् च जायते) 13. 109. 25.
आषाढी: Āṣāḍhī f.: Name of the full moon day in the month of Āṣāḍha. Virūpākṣa, the king of the Rākṣasas, used to give excellent and well-garnished food, as desired, to many Brāhmaṇas on every full moon day (पौर्णमास्याम् 12. 165. 16) of the month of Āṣāḍha (तस्य नित्यं तथा-षाढ्यां … बहवो द्विजाः । ईप्सितं भोजन-वरं लभन्ते सत्कृतं सदा) 12. 165. 15.
आकाशगङ्गा: Ākāśagaṅgā f.: The river Gaṅgā flow-ing in the sky, also called simply Gaṅgā (18. 3. 37, 39). A. Description: Holy (पुण्या) 18. 3. 26, 39; its waters described as holy (पुण्यं  … तोयम्) 12. 315. 46; the river of the gods (देवनदी) 18. 3. 26, 39; one that purifies the three worlds (त्रैलोक्यपावनी) 18. 3. 26; purifying (पावनी) 18. 3. 39; praised by the sages (ऋषिसंस्तुता) 18. 3. 39; flowing in the three worlds (त्रिलोकगा) 18. 3. 39. B. Location in the sky: The sixth wind known as Parivaha supports the holy waters of the Ākāśagaṅgā (पुण्यं चाकाशगङ्-गायास् तोयं विष्टभ्य तिष्ठति … षष्ठः परिवहो नाम स वायुः) 12. 315. 46, 48 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 328. 46: तोयं विष्टभ्य आकाशे एवावस्थाप्य). C. Epic event: Indra advised Yudhiṣṭhira to bathe in the Ākāśagaṅgā before proceeding to heaven 18. 3. 26; accordingly he went to the Gaṅgā and bathed there; having plunged in its water he gave up his human body, assumed a divine form and was free of the feelings of enmity and sorrow 18. 3. 37-40. D. My-thological event: Formerly the sage Bhara-dvāja, having gone to the Ākāśagaṅgā, was performing religious ablution (उपास्पृशन्); at that time he was touched by Viṣṇu who was taking his three steps (त्रीन् क्रमान् क्रमता विष्णुनाभ्यासादितः) 12. 329. 42. E. Importance: When Yudhiṣṭhira bathes in the Ākāśagaṅgā he will be free of his human existence, he will be relived of grief and fatigue and his feelings of enmity will disappear (अत्र स्नातस्य तो भावो मानुषो विगमिष्यति । गतशोको निरायासो मुक्तवैरो भविष्यसि) 18. 3. 27.
आदित्यतीर्थ: Ādityatīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: On the river Sarasvatī (तस्मिंस् तीर्थे सरस्वत्याः) 9. 48. 20; near the hermitage of Āditya (आदितस्याश्रमो यत्र; the तीर्थ not directly named) 3. 81. 160. B. Description: auspicious (शिव) 9. 48. 20; holy (पुण्य) 9. 48. 20; excellent among the तीर्थस् (तीर्थप्रवर) 9. 48. 21; best (उत्तम) 9. 48. 21; famous in the three worlds (त्रैलोक्यविश्रुत) 3. 81. 160 (the तीर्थ not directly named). C. Various events, mythological and others, associated with it: (1) God Sun, offered a sacrifice there, and obtained sovereignty over luminous bodies and prowess (ज्योतिषाम् आधिपत्यं च प्रभावं चाभ्यपध्यत) 9. 48. 17; (2) Formerly, Viṣṇu, after killing the demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha, bathed in this excellent तीर्थ (for purification ?) 9. 48. 21; (3) Near that तीर्थ, on the bank of the river Sarasvatī, are present all gods with Indra, the Viśvedevas together with the Maruts, the Gandharvas and the Apsarases, the Yakṣas, the Rākṣasas and the Piśācas, (Kṛṣṇa) Dvaipāyaṇa, Śukra, Kṛṣṇa and many others by thousands who have acquired perfection through योग 9. 48. 18-20; (4) (Kṛṣṇa) Dvaipāyana acquired the highest योग and the ultimate perfection by bathing in the Ādityatīrtha (संप्राप्तः परमं योगं सिद्धिं च परमां गतः) 9. 48. 22; (5) The sage Asita Devala too, (having bathed) in the same (तीर्थ,) and having practised meditation of a high quality, obtain-ed योग (असितो देवलश् चैव तस्मिन्न् एव महातपाः । परमं योगम् आस्थाय ऋषिर् योगम् अवाप्तवान्) 9. 48. 23. D. Im-portance: By bathing in the Ādityatīrtha (not directly named) and by worshipping god Sun (विभावसुम्) one goes to the world of Āditya and saves his own family (आदित्य-लोकं व्रजति कुलं चैव समुद्धरेत्) 3. 81. 161.
आपःप्रपतन: Āpaḥprapatana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। According to the Tīrthavaṃśa, narrated by Aṇgiras to Gautama (13. 26. 3-4), one who bathes in the तीर्थ is waited upon by the Apsarases (सेव्यते सो ऽप्सरोगणिः) 13. 26. 26.
आपगा: Āpagā1 f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Flowing to the east of the Mānuṣatīrtha at a distance of one क्रोश from it (मानुषस्य तु पूर्वेण क्रोश-मात्रे) 3. 81. 55. B. Description: Famous (विख्यात) 3. 81. 55; frequented by the Siddhas (सिद्धनिषेवित) 3. 81. 55. C. Importance: One who offers food made of श्यामाक grain to gods and manes obtains high religious merit; if one Brāhmaṇa is fed there, it is as good as feeding a crore of them (श्यामाकभोजनं तत्र यः प्रयच्-छति मानवः । देवान् पितॄंश् च उद्दिश्य तस्य धर्मफलं महत् । एकस्मिन् भोजिते विप्रे कोटिर् भवति भोजिता) 3. 81. 56; by bathing there, and by worshipping gods and manes, and by spending there one night one obtains the fruit of performing an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice 3. 81. 57.

Āpagā2 f.: Name of a river (could it be Gaṅgā ? cf. गङ्गाह्रदश् च तत्रैव 3. 81. 153). By bathing in Āpagā and by worshipping Maheśvara one becomes the chief of the Gaṇas of Śiva (? becomes a worshipper of Gaṇeśa ?) and rescues his own family (गाणपत्यम् अवाप्नोति कुलं चोद्धरते स्वकम्) 3. 81. 154.
Āpagā3 f.: Name of a river. Near the city Śākala in the Bāhlīka country (शाकलं नाम नगरम् आपगा नाम निम्नगा । जर्तिका नाम बाह्लिकास् तेषां वृत्तं सुनिन्दितम्) 8. 30. 14.
आर्चीकपर्वत: Ārcīkaparvata m.: Name of a moun-tain. A. Description: It has fruits in all the seasons (सदाफल) and it has streams flowing throughout the year (सदास्रोत) 3. 125. 13. B. Inhabitants: It is the abode of sages, and the highest station of the Maruts (निवासो वै मनीषिणाम् … मरु-तां स्थानम् उत्तमम्) 3. 125. 13. C. Structures: There were hundreds of struc-tures sacred to gods on it (चैत्याश् चैतेबहु-शतास् त्रिदशानां युधिष्ठिर) 3. 125. 13. D. Other important features: (1) It had three holy peaks and three waterfalls (शृङ्-गाणि त्रीणी पुण्यानि त्रीणि प्रस्रवणानि च) 3. 125. 15; Lomaśa advised the Pāṇḍavas to go around them in succession and bathe in them 3. 125. 15; (2) Here flew Yamunā whose current never dried up (यमुना चाक्षयस्रोताः) 3. 125. 18; (3) There was the तीर्थ of Candramas visited by sages, the Vaikhānasas and the Vālakhilyas 3. 125. 14. E. Place for practising austerities and for offering religious rites: (1) Gods and manes, together with great sages, always rested (नित्यशयाः) there and practised austerities; Yudhiṣṭhira was advised by Lomaśa to wor-ship them 3. 125. 17; (2) These gods and manes and the sages ate चरुस् (offered in sacrifices) 3. 125. 18; (3) Kṛṣṇa practised austerities on the mountain (कृष्णश् चेह त-पोरतः) 3. 125. 18; (4) Śaṃtanu, Śunaka, Nara and Nārāyaṇa acquired the eternal place (by practising austerities) here (स्थानं प्राप्ताः सनातनम्) 3. 125. 16; (5) Lomaśa suggested to the Pāṇḍavas that he and all of them should practise austerities and become very thin (सर्वे चात्र गमिष्यामः सुकृशाः सुतपस्विनः) 3. 125. 19.
आथर्वणस्य: Ātharvaṇasya sthānam nt.: Name of a place. One of the places seen by Arjuna when he and Kṛṣṇa journeyed at night to Hima-vant to propitiate Śiva for his Pāśupata (स्थानम् आथर्वणस्य च) 7. 57. 28.
आदित्यबन्धन: Ādityabandhana nt.: Name of the आश्रम of Vṛṣadhvaja (Śiva). A. Location: Situated to the north of Himavant (उत्तरां दिशं गत्वा शैल-राजस्य पार्श्वतः) 12. 314. 18. B. Ex-tent: Its extent was ten योजनस् (दशयो-जनविस्तारम्) 12. 314. 20. C. Chara-cteristics: (1) Vṛṣadhvaja constantly practised austerities in this आश्रम (तपो ऽतप्यत दुर्धर्षस् तात नित्यं व्र्षध्व-जः) 12. 314. 18, 22; (2) It is encircled by blazing fire and hence inaccessible to those who have not controlled their self (पावकेन परिक्षिप्तो दीप्यता तस्य चाश्र-मः । आदित्यबन्धनं नाम दुर्धर्षम् अकृतात्मभिः) 12. 314. 19; (अग्निज्वाला-समावृतम्) 12. 314. 20; God Fire himself is present there to destroy all obstacles to the austerities of Mahādeva (भगवान् पावकस् तत्र स्वयं तिष्ठति वीर्यवान् । सर्वविघ्नान् प्रशमयन् महादेवस्य धी-मतः ॥ ) 12. 314. 21; (3) Yakṣas, Rākṣa-sas, and Dānavas cannot go there 12. 314. 20.
आदित्यस्य: Ādityasya āśramaḥ m.: Name of an आश्रम। The आश्रम of the high-souled Āditya (sun), the store of lustre, situated near the Ādityatīrtha (आदित्यस्याश्रमो यत्र तेजो-राशेर् महात्मनः) 3. 81. 160. [See Aditya-tīriha Vol. I. 293-294]
आश्रम: Āśramaḥ m.: An आश्रम, name of which is not mentioned; it once belonged to Viṣṇu and then to the daughter of Śāṇḍilya. A. Location: To the north of Kuru-kṣetra, near the Himavant mountain (पार्श्वे हिमवतः) 9. 53. 9, 1. B. Description: Holy, having holy characteristics (पुण्य) 9. 53. 2, 9, (पुण्यलक्षण) 9. 53. 3; hea-venly (दिव्य) 9. 53. 1; excellent, excellent आश्रम (प्रवर) 9. 53. 3, (आश्रमवर) 9. 53. 3; extensive (सुमहन्त्) 9. 53. 1; having Madhūka, Āmra, Plakṣa, Nyagro-dha, Ciribilva, Panasa and Arjuna trees in very large number (मधूकाम्रवनोपेतं प्लक्षन्यग्रोधसंकुलम् । चिरिबिल्वयुतं पुण्यं पनसार्जुनसंकुलम् ॥ ) 9. 53. 2. C. Epic event: Balarāma visited it after seeing Kurukṣetra and asked the sages whose आश्रम it was; Balarāma, after listening to their account, bowed down to them and went up the Himavant mountain 9. 53. 1, 3, 9. D. Past event: The sages when asked by Balarāma whose आश्रम it was told him to whom the आश्रम formerly belonged (यस्यायं पूर्वम् आश्रमः) 9. 53. 4: (1) Formerly Viṣṇu practised in the आश्रम the best austerities and performed according to rites all the ancient sacrifices (अत्र विष्णुः पुरा देवस् तप्तवांस् तप उत्तमम् । अत्रास्य विधिवद् यज्ञाः सर्वे वृत्ताः सनातनाः) 9. 53. 5; (2) The dau-ghter of Śāṇḍilya who observed chastity since her maidenhood (कौमारब्रह्म-चारिणी) practised austerities there; she enjoyed in the आश्रम the fruit of the Aśva-medha sacrifice (भुक्त्वाश्रमे ऽश्वमेध-स्य फलम्) and then taking recourse to योग went to heaven (योगयुक्ता दिवं याता; सा तु प्राप्य परं योगं गता स्वर्गम्) 9. 53. 6-8.
आश्रमः: Āśramaḥ m.: An आश्रम, name of which is not mentioned; it once belonged to Viṣṇu and then to the daughter of Śāṇḍilya. A. Location: To the north of Kuru-kṣetra, near the Himavant mountain (पार्श्वे हिमवतः) 9. 53. 9, 1. B. Description: Holy, having holy characteristics (पुण्य) 9. 53. 2, 9, (पुण्यलक्षण) 9. 53. 3; hea-venly (दिव्य) 9. 53. 1; excellent, excellent आश्रम (प्रवर) 9. 53. 3, (आश्रमवर) 9. 53. 3; extensive (सुमहन्त्) 9. 53. 1; having Madhūka, Āmra, Plakṣa, Nyagro-dha, Ciribilva, Panasa and Arjuna trees in very large number (मधूकाम्रवनोपेतं प्लक्षन्यग्रोधसंकुलम् । चिरिबिल्वयुतं पुण्यं पनसार्जुनसंकुलम् ॥ ) 9. 53. 2. C. Epic event: Balarāma visited it after seeing Kurukṣetra and asked the sages whose आश्रम it was; Balarāma, after listening to their account, bowed down to them and went up the Himavant mountain 9. 53. 1, 3, 9. D. Past event: The sages when asked by Balarāma whose आश्रम it was told him to whom the आश्रम formerly belonged (यस्यायं पूर्वम् आश्रमः) 9. 53. 4: (1) Formerly Viṣṇu practised in the आश्रम the best austerities and performed according to rites all the ancient sacrifices (अत्र विष्णुः पुरा देवस् तप्तवांस् तप उत्तमम् । अत्रास्य विधिवद् यज्ञाः सर्वे वृत्ताः सनातनाः) 9. 53. 5; (2) The dau-ghter of Śāṇḍilya who observed chastity since her maidenhood (कौमारब्रह्म-चारिणी) practised austerities there; she enjoyed in the आश्रम the fruit of the Aśva-medha sacrifice (भुक्त्वाश्रमे ऽश्वमेध-स्य फलम्) and then taking recourse to योग went to heaven (योगयुक्ता दिवं याता; सा तु प्राप्य परं योगं गता स्वर्गम्) 9. 53. 6-8.
आश्रमपद: Āśramapada nt.: The precincts of an आश्रम (not named). A. Location: On the confluence of Gaṅgā and Yamunā (आश्रमपदं गङ्गा-यमुनसंगमे) 5. 118. 1. B. Descrip-tion: Nāgas, Yakṣas and men gathered there, as also birds (पतत्रिन् and पक्षिन्, big and small birds ?), deer, and forest-dwellers who lived on mountain trees; the forest near the आश्रम was thronged by kings of different peoples and countries and by sages who resembled Brahman (नागयक्षम-नुष्याणां पतत्रिमृगपक्षिणाम् । शैलद्रु-मवनौकानाम् आसीत् तत्र समागमः ॥ नानापुरुषदेशानाम् ईश्वरैश् च समाकुलम् । ऋषिभिर् ब्रह्मकल्पैश् च समन्ताद् आवृतं वनम् ॥ ) 5. 118. 3-4. C. Past event: King Yayāti, wishing to arrange, the स्व-यंवर of his daughter Mādhavī a second time, went to this Āśramapada (उपगम्या-श्रमपदम्); Puru and Yadu, his two sons, took their sister there in a chariot (रथम् आरोप्य माधवीम् पुरुर् यदुश् च भगिनीम् आश्रमे पर्यधावताम्) 5. 118. 2.
आश्रममण्डल: Āśramamaṇḍala nt.: A group of आश्रमस् (not named). A. Location; Situated on the bank of Yamunā (प्रविश्याश्रममण्डलम् । य-मुनातीरम् आश्रित्य) 5. 187. 18; (यमुना-तीरम् आसाद्य) 5. 187. 20. B. Epic event: Ambā entered the Āśramamaṇḍala to pra-ctise severe austerities in order to be able to kill Bhīṣma 5. 187. 18.
आसन्दी: Āsandī f.: Name of a village (ग्राम). One of the five villages for five Pāṇḍa-vas in return of which Yudhiṣṭhira was prepared to have peace with the Kauravas; four of these five villages—Kuśasthala, Vṛkasthala, Āsandī and Vāraṇāvata—were actually named by Yudhiṣṭhira; he left to Duryodhana to name the fifth (किंचिद् एव तु पञ्चमम्) 5. 31. 19; (भ्रातॄणाम् देहि पञ्चानां ग्रामान् पञ्च सुयोधन । शान्तिर् नो ऽस्तु) 5. 31. 20; (पञ्च ग्रामा वृता मया) 5. 70. 14-15; (पञ्च नस् तात दीय-न्तां ग्रामा वा नगराणि वा) 5. 70. 16; 5. 80. 7.
आजमीढ: Ājamīḍha m. (pl.): The descendants of Ajamīḍha, the family of Ajamīḍha. Epic events: (1) All the kings who had gathered for the Rājasūya congratu-lated Yudhiṣṭhira on completion of the sacrifice and said that he augmented the fame of Ājamīḍhas (आजमीढानां यशः संवर्धितं त्वया) 2. 42. 36; (2) Kṛṣṇa referred to Kuntī who, as daughter of Śūra (and wife of Pāṇḍu), had gone over to the Ājamīḍha family (शूरस्य राज्ञो दुहिता आजमीढकुलं गता) 5. 88. 90; (3) Drau-padī referred to herself as the daughter of Drupada who, as the chief queen of the Pāṇḍavas, had gone to the Ājamīḍha family (सुता द्रुपदराजस्य … आजमीढ-कुलं प्राप्ता … महिषी पाण्डुपुत्राणाम्) 5. 80. 22.
आज्यप: Ājyapa m. (pl.): A class of deities. Mentioned by Kṛṣṇa among those gods who were the creation of Śiva (देवाः … आज्यपाश् च ॥ … शर्वाज् जातं विद्धि तत् कीर्तितं मे ॥ ) 13. 18. 51, 53.
आत्रेय: Ātreya m. (sg., pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and a family of ऋषिस्। (1) Janapada: One of the northern Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa listed by Saṃjaya (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (उत्तराश् च) 6. 10. 63; (आत्रेयाः सभरद्वाजाः) 6. 10. 67; (2) Ṛṣis: The Atreyas are describ-ed as those who observed the best vows (आत्रेयाश् चोत्तमव्रताः) 3. 27. 8; they are listed by Baka Dālbhya among the Brāh-maṇas who gathered around Yudhiṣṭhira in Dvaitavana 3. 27. 1, 5; all the Brāhmaṇas are said to be ascetics; they observed vows in the holy Dvaita forest and practised धर्म under the protection of Yudhi-ṣṭhira; they were also the best Brāhmaṇas in the whole world (पश्य द्वैतवने पार्थ ब्राह्मणानां तपस्विनाम् । … चरन्ति धर्मं पुण्ये ऽस्मिंस् त्वया गुप्ता धृत-व्रताः । … सर्वस्य जगतः श्रेष्ठा ब्राह्-मणाः संगतास् त्वया) 3. 27. 7-8; the sound of the loud recitation of the यजुस्, ऋच्, सामन्स् and of prose formulae was pleasing (यजुषाम् ऋचाम् च साम्नां च गद्यानां चैव सर्वशः । आसीद् उच्चार्य-माणानां निस्वनो हृदयंगमः ॥ ) 3. 27. 3; (3) Ṛṣis who were descendants of Atri: (i) Kuṇḍajaṭhara (आत्रेयः कुण्ड-जठरः) 1. 48. 8; (ii) Kauṇḍinya (आत्रे-यस् त्व् अथ कौण्डिन्यः) 3. 83. 102.
आदिदाय: Ādidāya m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people. One of the southern Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa listed by Saṃjaya for the in-formation of Dhṛtarāṣṭra (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10, 37. 5; (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणाः) 6. 10. 56; (आदिदायाः सिरालाश् च) 6. 10. 62.
आदिराष्ट्र: Ādirāṣṭra m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (आदिराष्ट्राः सुकुट्टाश् च) 6. 10. 43; also called देश (उद्देशमात्रेण मया देशाः संकीर्तिताः) 6. 10. 68.
आनर्त: Ānarta m. (pl., once sg. 3. 180. 25): Name of a country and its people. A. Location: One of the (northern) Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa listed by Saṃjaya (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (तथैवानर्त-नैरृताः) 6. 10. 50; also called देश 6. 10. 68; (for its location in the north also see the next section Epic Events 1); country in which Dvārakā was located (यद्य् अहं द्वारकायां स्याम्) 3. 14. 1; (असांनिध्यं तु कौरव्य ममा-नर्तेष्व् अभूत् तदा) 3. 14. 14. B. Epic events: (1) Arjuna, in his expedition to the north before the Rājasūya, conquered it (विजयाय प्रयास्यामि दिशं धनद-रक्षिताम्) 2. 23. 4; (दिशं धनपतेर् इष्टाम् अजयत् पाकशासनिः) 2. 23. 9; (आनर्-तान् कालकूटांश् च … विजित्य सः) 2. 23. 14; (3) Śālva, who attacked Dvārakā in the absence of Kṛṣṇa (3. 14. 14; 3. 15. 5), asked the people of the Ānarta country to tell him the truth about the whereabouts of Kṛṣṇa (आनर्ताः सत्यम् आख्यात तत्र गन्तास्मि यत्र सः) 3. 15. 9; (4) Kṛṣṇa was enraged at the destruction of Ānarta by Śālva and Śālva's reviling him (आन्तर्-तेषु विमर्दं च क्षेपं चात्मनि कौरव  … तस्य दुष्कृतकर्मणः) 3. 15. 18; (5) The actors, dancers and singers of the Ānarta country were asked to leave (the town Dvārakā) when it was fortified to resist the attack by Śālva (आनर्ताश् च तथा सर्वे नटनर्तकगायनाः । बहिर् विवासिताः सर्वे) 3. 16. 14; (6) Pradyu-mna reassured the army of the Ānarta warriors who were afraid when they saw Śālva in his Saubha alighting on the earth (व्यवस्थाप्य च तद् बलम् । आनर्तानां महाराज प्रद्युम्नो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥ ) 3. 17. 29-31; (7) Kṛṣṇa comforted Drau-padī by telling her that her sons had procee-ded towards Ānarta and had entered the city of Dvārakā; there they were not envious of gods (आनर्तम् एवाभिमुखाः … गत्वा … तवात्मजा वृष्णिपुरं प्रविश्य न दैवतेभ्यः स्पृहयन्ति कृष्णे) 3. 180. 25; (8) Arjuna brought Janārdana, Dāśārhas and Abhimanyu to Upaplavya from the Ānarta country for the marriage of Abhi-manyu with Uttarā (बीभत्सुर् आनिनाय जनार्दनम् । आनर्तेभ्यो ऽपि दाशार्हान् अभि-मन्युं च पाण्डवः ॥ ) 4. 67. 15; (9) According to Yudhiṣṭhira Kuntī was respe-cted by the people of the Ānarta country (आनर्तसत्कृता) 5. 81. 45; (10) Viviṃ-śati killed hundreds of Ānarta warriors in the battle but was himself later killed (विविंशतिर् … आनर्तयोधाञ् शतशो निहत्य निहतो रणे) 8. 4. 7; (11) Kṛtavarman, a resident of Ānarta country, listed by Saṃjaya among those who survived the death of Karṇa (आनर्तवासी हृदिकात्मजो ऽसौ … कृतवर्मा) 8. 4. 92; (12) Yudhi-ṣṭhira permitted Kṛṣṇa to return to his country to meet the Ānarta people and his father; Kṛṣṇa then returned to the Ānartanagarī (i. e. Dvārakā) (आनर्तान् अवलोक्य त्वं पितरं च महाभुज) 14. 51. 46; (ततो ययौ … जनार्दनः … आनर्त-पुरीम्) 14. 51. 56.
आभीर: Ābhīra m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people. A. Location: Mentioned by Saṃjaya among the Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (आभीराः कालतोयकाः) 6. 10. 45; counted by him among the nor-thern Mleccha people (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना भरतसत्तम) 6. 10. 63; (शूद्राभीराथ दरदाः) 6. 10. 66; they are called residents of Pañcanada (आभिरैः  … पञ्चनदालयैः) 16. 9. 16; (also cf. स पञ्चनदम् आसाद्य 16. 8. 43); in the description of the expedition of Nakula to the west of Khāṇḍavaprastha (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीं अभितो दिशम् 2. 29. 2) Ābhīras are said to live on the bank of the river Sarasvatī (शूद्राभीरगणाश् चैव ये चाश्रित्य सरस्वतीम्) 2. 29. 9. B. Characteristics: They are called Mlecchas 16. 8. 61; Dasyus 16. 8. 44, 47, 58, 60; they live on fish (वर्तयन्ति च ये मत्स्यैर् … ) 2. 29. 9; fight with sticks (यष्टिप्रहरणाः) 16. 8. 47; plunderers (लोप्त्रहारिणः) 16. 8. 47; evil doers (पापकर्माणः) 16. 8. 45; greedy (लोभोपहतचेतसः) 16. 8. 45; whose sight was inauspicious (अशुभदर्श-नाः) 16. 8. 45; who did not know धर्म (अधर्मज्ञाः) 16. 8. 50; who did not follow the correct course (मूढाः) 16. 8. 51. C. Epic events: (1) Nakula in his expedi-tion to the west before the Rājasūya brought, among others, the clans of Ābhīras under his control (शूद्राभीरगणाश् चैव … वशे चक्रे) 2. 29. 9-10; (2) They fought on the side of the Kauravas; on the twelfth day of the war they were placed at the neck of the Suparṇa Vyūha (7. 19. 4-5) arranged by Droṇa (शूराभीरा दशेरकाः । … ग्रीवायाम्) 7. 19. 7; (3) When Arjuna reached Pañca-nada along with men and women of the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas (16. 8. 33-38, 43), the Ābhīras consulted among themselves and knowing that Arjuna was the only warrior to escort the women, thousands of them, equipped with sticks, attacked Bhojas and others to loot their wealth; they did not mind the threats of Arjuna and kidnapped the women under his charge; Arjuna struck some of them with his arrows and when the arrows were exhausted he killed the Dasyus with the tip of his bow; but the Mlecchas succeeded in taking away with them Vṛṣṇi women in spite of Arjuna's effort to protect them (आभीरा मन्त्रयाम् आसुह् समेत्याशुभदर्-शनाः ॥ अयम् एको ऽर्जुनो योद्धा … । नयत्य् अस्मान् अतिक्रम्य … ॥ ततो यष्टिप्रहरणा दस्यवस् ते सहस्रशः । अभ्यधावन्त वृष्णीनाम् तं जनं … ॥ तथोक्तास् तेन वीरेण कदर्थीकृत्य तद्वचः । अभिपेतुर् जनं … । … शरैह् पार्थो … ।जघान दस्यून् … ॥ … धनुष्कोट्या तदा दस्यून् अव-धीत् पाकशासनिः ॥ प्रेक्षतस् त्व् एव पार्थ-स्य वृष्ण्यन्धकवरस्त्रियः । जग्मुर् आदाय ते म्लेच्छाः । ) 16. 8. 43-61; Arjuna repor-ted the abduction of Vṛṣṇi women by Ābhiras to Vyāsa (पश्यतो वृष्णिदाराश् च मम ब्रह्मन् सहस्रशः । आभीरैर् अनु-सृत्याजौ हृताः) 16. 9. 16. D. Past event: Sarasvatī formerly disappeared at Vinaśana due to her hatred for Śūdras and Ābhīras (ततो विनशनं … । शूद्राभीरान् प्रति द्वेषाद् यत्र नष्टा सरस्वती) 9. 36. 1. E. They figure in a prophecy; While describing the end of the Kali era to Yudhiṣṭhira, Mārkaṇ-ḍeya counted Ābhīras among the Mleccha kings who would rule the earth (बहवो म्लेच्छराजानः पृथिव्यां मनुजाधिप ।  … शूद्रास् तथाभीरा नरोत्तम) 3. 186. 29, 30.
आमरथ: Āmaratha m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada (?) Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (वातजामरथोरगाः) 6. 10. 53 (Or is this to be read as वातजाम-रथोरगाः ?)
आरट्ट: Āraṭṭa, Bāhlī̆ka m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people; also referred to as Pañcanada (8. 30. 62, 65-66, 74), Āraṭṭaka (8. 30. 74), Bāhlī̆ (2. 47. 22; 5. 84. 6; 13. 106. 16), Jartika (8. 30. 14); perhaps also as Bāhyālaya (? 8. 30. 61). A. Name: Āraṭṭa (आरट्टा नाम ते देशाः) 8. 30. 36; (आरट्टजान्) 6. 81. 31; Bāhlīka (बाह्लीकदेशम्) 8. 30. 9; Bāhli (बाह्लिजातानाम् 13. 106. 16; बाह्लिजातैः 5. 84. 6); Āraṭṭa and Bāhlīka identified (आरट्टा नाम बाह्लीकाः) 8. 30. 40, 43; as people, the two are enumerated separately (आरट्ट-बाह्लिकैः) 6. 71. 16; 7. 35. 36; 7. 97. 26; 7. 132. 24; 7. 165. 79; once they are distin-guished-Āraṭṭa as the name of the country, Bāhlīka, as the name of the people (आरट्टा नाम ते देशा बह्लीका नाम ते जनाः) 8. 30. 47; for Bāhlīka as name of the people, cf. Śalya is called बाह्लीकपुंगवः 1. 61. 6; Somadatta as बाह्लिकानां ऋषभः 5. 30. 19; but the people are also called Āraṭṭaka 8. 30. 74, or simply Āraṭṭa 6. 71. 16, Āraṭṭā (f.) 8. 30. 58; name Bāhlī̆ for Bāhlīka, probably due to metrical reasons 2. 47. 22; 13. 106. 16; since the country was marked by five rivers (see Section C. Location below), it was also known as Pañcanada 8. 30. 62, 74; (धर्मं पाञ्चनदम्) 8. 30. 65-66; name Bāhyālaya is doubtful; the text reads प्रायो बाह्या लयाद् ऋते (8. 30. 61) (Arjunamiśra explains प्रायो बाह्या यथोक्तप्रदेशबहिर्भूताः । लयात् मद्र-देशात्, see Cr. Ed. Vol. 10, p. 267, Cr. App. for 8. 30. 61); perhaps the text is to be read as बाह्यालयाद् ऋते 'except those who have their residence outside (the countries Kurus, Pāñcālas etc. just mentioned before); also cf. Editor's note on the stanza Cr. Ed. Vol. 10. p. 687). B. Explanation of the name: A certain Brāhmaṇa had informed the Kuru assembly that there were two Piśācas named Bahi and Hlīka living on the river Vipāśā; Bāhlikas were their progeny; they were not Prajāpati's creation (यद् अन्यो ऽप्य् उक्तवान् सभ्यो ब्राह्मणः कुरुसंसदि । … बहिश् च नाम ह्लीकश् च विपाशायां पिशाचकौ । तयोर् अपत्यं बाह्लीका नैषा सृष्टिः प्रजापतेः ॥ 8. 30. 41, 44; (of the two Piśācas, Bahi was female, Hlīka, male, see Cr. Ed. Vol. 10 p. 687). C. (21) During the night war, Arjuna killed many Āraṭṭa Kṣatriyas (यौधेया-रट्टराजन्यान् … युधि । प्राहिणोन् मृत्यु-लोकाय किरीटी) 7. 136. 5; (22) Afraid, Bāhlikas respected Karṇa's lack of confu-sion while fighting with Ghaṭotkaca (ततो भीताः समुदैक्षन्त कर्णं … बाह्लिकाश् च । असंमोहं पूजयन्तो ऽस्य संख्ये) 7. 154. 45; (23) On the fifteenth day of war, Dhṛṣṭadyumna scattered away Bāhlīkas protecting Droṇa (स … बाह्लीकान् … रक्षि-ष्यमाणान् संग्रामे द्रोणं व्यधमद् अच्युतः ॥ ) 7. 165. 24; (24) After the death of Droṇa, Kṛtavarman, surrounded by Āraṭṭa and Bāhlika warriors left the battlefield with their swift horses (कलिङ्गा-रट्टबाह्लिकैः । कृतवर्मा वृतो राजन् प्रायात् सुजवनैर् हयैः ॥ ) 7. 165. 79; (25) Saṃjaya told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that king Bāhlika, his grand-father (1. 90. 46), toge-ther with his Bāhlika warriors was killed by Bhīma (पितामहस् तव तथा बाह्लिकस् सह बाह्लिकैः । भीमसेनेन विक्रम्य गमितो यमसादनम् ॥ ) 8. 4. 30 (reference to 7. 132. 15); (26) Horse-riding Bāhlīkas, fighting with शक्ति, प्रास अन्द् तुणीर, along with their horses, killed by the Pāṇḍya king (सशक्तिप्रासतूणीरान् अश्वारोहान् हयान् अपि … °बाह्लीकान् … क्रूरान् संग्रामकर्-कशान् । पाण्ड्यो ऽकरोद् व्यसून्) 8. 15. 9-10; (27) Karṇa told Śalya what an old Brāhmaṇa, who had lived long in Bāhlīka country and hence was conversant with their way of life, said to Dhṛtarāṣṭra while reviling the Bāhlīka country and its people (तत्र वृद्धः … द्विजोत्तमः । बाह्लीक-देशं … कुत्सयन् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥ … बाह्लीकेषूषितं मया । तत एषां समा-चारः संवासाद् विदितो मम ॥ ) 8. 30. 9, 13, 27; other Brāhmaṇas too reviled Bāhlīkas in the Kuru assembly (यद् अन्यो ऽप्य् उक्तवान् अस्मान् ब्राह्मणः कुरुसंसदि) 8. 30. 34, 38; 8. 30. 41; (यद् अप्य् अन्यो ऽब्रवीद् वाक्यं बाह्लीकानां विकुत्सितम्) 8. 30. 57; Karṇa also told Śalya what he had heard about a Brāhmaṇa reviling Bāhlīkas when he was the guest of an artisan (ब्रा-ह्मणः … शिल्पिनम् अब्रवीत्) 8. 30. 48-49; Karṇa told Śalya what Rākṣasa Kalmāṣa-pāda said about Bāhlīkas (कल्माषपादः  … राक्षसो ऽब्रवीत्) 8. 30. 67; (28) Arjuna said that he would burn Bāhlikas with the fire of his arrows (शरार्चिषा गाण्डिवेनाहम् एकः । … बाह्लिकांश् चाभिपत्य॑ … दहेयं सगणान् प्रसह्य) 8. 52. 32 [See Madra, and Śākala city Vol. II. 1. 5A. p. 573]
आरेवक: Ārevaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the second day of the war Ārevaka warriors and Trigartas, along with others led by Duḥśāsana, were to protect Bhīṣma (आरेवकास् त्रिगर्ताश् च … सहितास् तथा दुःशासनेन च । … भीष्मम् एवाभिरक्ष-न्तु) 6. 47. 7-9.
आर्य: Ārya m. (pl.): Designation of a people. A. Location: One of the three kinds of people who live in the Bhāratavarṣa (अत्र ते वर्णयीष्यामि वर्षं भारत भारतम्) 6. 10. 5, 9; (आर्या म्लेच्छाश् च तैर् मिश्राः पुरुषा विभो) 6. 10. 12; they drink water of rivers like Gaṅgā, Sindhu and Sarasvatī (नदीः पिबन्ति बहुला गङ्गां सिन्धुं सरस्वतीम्) 6. 10. 13. B. Characteristics: (1) The Āryas do not use irregular gramma-tical forms in their speech, they do not play tricks; they do not fight croockedly, nor employ deceipt; this was the way of life of the righteous persons (नार्या म्लेच्छन्ति भाषाभिर् मायया न चरन्त्य् उत । अजिह्-मम् अशठं य्न्द्धम् एतत् सत्पुरुषव्र-तं) 2. 53. 8; (2) According to the Āryas it was best and proper to be able to say: “If reviled, I shall keep quiet; if beaten, I shall always forgive”; truth, straightforwardness and kindness was best and proper in their opinion (आक्रुश्यमाणो न वदामि किंचित् क्षमाम्य् अहम् ताड्यमानश् च नित्यम् । श्रेष्ठं ह्य् एतत् क्षमम् अप्य् आहुर् आर्याः सत्यं तथैवार्जवम् आनृशंस्यम् ॥ (12. 288. 12), (3) One should be in a posi-tion to say: “I always wait upon Āryas patiently (सदाहम् आर्यान् निभृतो ऽप्य् उपासे) 12. 288. 19; (4) The Āryas by controlling (their longing for) objects of senses and by abandoning darkness arising out of igno-rance had taken the northern path and reached the regions of those who renounced everything (उत्तरेण तु पन्थानम् आर्या विषयनिग्रहात् । अबुद्धिजं तमस् त्यक्त्वा लोकांस् त्यागवतां गताः ॥ ) 12. 19. 13. C. Epic events: (1) The Āryas and the Mlecchas who had seen or heard about the difficult life of the Pāṇḍavas shed tears before the war started (म्लेच्छाश् चार्याश् च ये तत्र ददृशुः शुश्रुवुस् तदा । वृत्तं तत् पाण्डुपुत्राणाम् रुरुदुस् ते) 6. 41. 103 (However, Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 43. 108; आर्याः कुलीनाः वृत्तं चरितम्); (2) When Sudakṣiṇa and Śrutāyudha were killed, Abhīṣāhas, Śūrasenas, Śibis and Vasātis rained arrows on Arjuna; Arjuna killed six thousand Āryas of them; afraid, first they ran away, but returned again and encircled Arjuna only to get killed by him (तेषां षष्टिशतान् आर्यान् प्रामथ्नात् पाण्डवः शरैः । ते स्म भीताः पलायन्त … ॥ ते निवृ-त्य पुनः पार्थं सर्वतः पर्यवारयन् । तेषाम् आपततां तूर्णं … शिरांसि पातयाम् आस बाहूंश् चैव धनंजयः ॥ ) 7. 68. 2-5; (3) When Arjuna accompanied the Aśva-medha horse, Ārya kings, together with delighted warriors and horses, went with him (आर्याश् च पृथिवीपालाः प्रहृष्टनरवा-हनाः । समीयुः पाण्डुपुत्रेण) 14. 72. 25.
आर्यावर्त: Āryāvarta m.: Name of a part (देश) of the Bhāratavarṣa. A. Location: Formed a part of the Bhāratavarṣa (स … भारतं वर्षम् आसदत्) 12. 312. 13-14. B. Past event: Śuka, while going to meet Janaka in Mithilā (in the Videha country) at the instance of Vyāsa (12. 312. 6, 12, 19), saw on way many countries inhabited by Cīnas and Hūṇas and then arrived at Āryāvarta (स देशान् विविधान् पश्यंश् चीनहूणनिषेवितान् । आर्या-वर्तम् इमं देशम् आजगाम महामुनिः) 12. 312. 15.
आहुक: Āhuka m. (pl.): Name of a people. Kṛṣṇa was called the chief of the Āhu-kas (आहुकानाम् अधिपतिः) 5. 84. 2.
आह्वायक: Āhvāyaka m. (pl.): A class of degraded Brāhmaṇas. They are among the five who were con-demned as Caṇḍālas among the Brāhmaṇas (आह्वायका देवलका नक्षत्रग्रामयाजकाः । एते ब्राह्मणचण्डाला महापथिकपञ्च-माः) 12. 77. 8; if the royal treasury be-came empty, a king should collect taxes from them (एतेभ्यो बलिम् आदद्याद् धीन-कोशो महीपतिः) 12. 77. 9; (They are pro-bably those who announced names in courts or executed court summons (?); Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 76. 6: आह्वायकाः धर्माधि-कारीणः).
आवह: Āvaha m.: Name of the second of the seven winds. A. Divine origin: All the seven winds are Aditi's sons ( … एते ऽदितेः पुत्रा मारुताः) 12. 315. 53. B. Description: All the seven winds are very wonderful; they blow incessantly everywhere sustain-ing all (creatures) (परमाद्भुताः । अनार-मन्तः संवान्ति सर्वगाः सर्वधारिणः) 12. 315. 53; Āvaha makes noise while blowing (नदन्) 12. 315. 37. C. Activity: There are seven paths of the winds which blow on the earth and in the atmosphere; Āvaha blows along the second path (पृथि-व्याम् अन्तरिक्षे च यत्र संवान्ति वायवः । सप्तैते वायुमार्गा वै) 12. 315. 31; (आवहो नाम संवाति द्वितीयः) 12. 315. 37; the Āvaha wind takes moisture from the clouds and excellent lustre from the lightnings while blowing in the sky (अम्बरे स्नेहम् अभ्रे-भ्यस् तडिद्भ्यश् चोत्तमा द्युतिः । आवहो नाम संवाति द्वितीयः श्वसनो नदन् ॥ ) 12. 315. 37.
